Name: Healthcare Cost Inflation
Description: Year-over-year change in medical care CPI component
Current Value: 3.1% overall (Mar 2026); services 3.7%; commodities 0.3%; hospital services +0.4% MoM; Rx drugs -1.5% MoM
Notes: Mar 2026: overall 3.1% (DOWN from 3.4% Feb, 3.2% Jan). Services component 3.7% — RISING. Commodities/Rx dragging overall index down (-1.5% MoM Rx). Gap vs employer 9-10% actual cost growth persists. General CPI 3.3% Mar — medical BELOW general for first time in recent trend. Services side still above threshold trajectory. Watch April CPI (May 12).

Name: Hospital Price Growth
Description: Year-over-year change in hospital services pricing
Current Value: ~3.5% CPI hospital component; actual charge growth higher
Data Sources: BLS Hospital CPI, HCCI, Kaufman Hall
Notes: CPI likely understates true hospital price growth. Consolidated markets pricing above inflation. Hospital median operating margin 1.3% Dec 2025 — margin recovery via pricing.

Name: Prescription Drug Cost Growth
Description: Year-over-year change in prescription drug costs (commercial/employer)
Current Value: 11-12% employer Rx trend projected 2026; GLP-1s primary driver (+30% from GLP-1 alone for covering employers)
Data Sources: Segal 2026 Cost Trend; PwC Behind the Numbers; KFF EHBS 2025
Notes: ELEVATED. GLP-1 drugs are single biggest Rx driver. IRA negotiation only helps Medicare (10 drugs). Commercial Rx continues double-digit growth. Specialty pipeline adds long-term structural pressure.

Name: OOP as Share of Income
Description: Household out-of-pocket healthcare spending as % of income
Current Value: Deductible alone = ~3% of $60K median income; add premium share = 5-7% for middle-income
Notes: Aggregate stat understates burden on bottom 60%. For households near deductible = 10%+ of income. Premium share growing too (+5-6% YoY in 2025).

Name: Average Deductible Burden
Description: Average annual deductible relative to median income
Current Value: $1,886 avg single; $2,631 small firms; $4,969 family; 53% small firm workers face $2,000+; 34% all workers face $2,000+
Threshold Critical: Exceeds liquid savings for median worker
Notes: +17% since 2020; +43% over decade. Core structural driver. $1,886 deductible = amount must be paid before insurance provides meaningful coverage. Median worker liquid savings ~$1,500 — deductible exceeds it.

Name: Catastrophic Cost Exposure
Description: Share of population functionally uninsured or underinsured
Current Value: 23% underinsured (Commonwealth Fund 2024); 8.2% fully uninsured (Census 2024); effectively 31%+ exposed
Notes: ACA subsidy lapse in 2026 pushing more into uninsured. Underinsurance disproportionately in employer-insured (66% of underinsured have employer coverage). Rising, not stable.

Name: Medical Debt Prevalence
Description: Share of adults with any medical debt
Current Value: 41% (KFF broad incl dental/medical); 20% (CFPB collections); 55% LendingTree incurred some at any point
Notes: CFPB rule vacated July 2025 — debt stays on credit reports. 15 states now have state-level reporting protections. Underlying debt burden unchanged despite credit bureau policy changes.

Name: Medical Debt in Collections
Description: Share of adults with medical debt in third-party collections
Current Value: 4.1% on credit reports (9.7M) — down from 27M due to credit bureau policy changes; $88B total outstanding
Notes: Apparent improvement is POLICY ARTIFACT from 2022 bureau changes (removed debts <$500, paid debts). CFPB rule to remove medical debt from reports was VACATED July 2025. Underlying burden unchanged. 15 state laws active.

Name: Average Medical Debt Balance
Description: Average medical debt balance among those with debt
Current Value: $88B / 20% adults ≈ ~$4,400 avg per person with collections debt
Notes: Rough estimate. Hospital traumatic injury study: +5.2pp jump in collections debt; +3.2/1000 bankruptcy filings within 15 months of injury. Single acute event is the trigger.

Name: Care Deferral Rate
Description: Share of adults who delayed or skipped care due to cost
Current Value: 36% (KFF Jan 2026); 33% (Gallup Nov 2025); 18% say health worsened; 66% worried about affordability (record)
Data Sources: KFF Health Tracking Poll Jan 2026; West Health-Gallup Nov 2025
Notes: ELEVATED and RISING. Above threshold. 18% health worsened = care deferral cascade ACTIVATING. 47% worried about 2026 costs is record high since 2021. State disparities: TX/MT/AK at 41-43%.

Name: Medication Non-Adherence Rate
Description: Share not taking medications as prescribed due to cost
Current Value: 20.2% (2022 survey — most recent); 12.9% delayed fills; 11.1% didn't fill; 7.9% skipped doses
Data Sources: National panel survey 2022; KFF, Commonwealth, CDC
Notes: At threshold. Causes $528B annual cost, 100K preventable deaths, 25% of hospitalizations. Insulin, cardiovascular, mental health highest risk. Needs 2025-2026 data refresh from newer survey.

Name: Unmet Healthcare Need
Description: Share with unmet healthcare need due to cost
Current Value: 11% "Cost Desperate" (West Health-Gallup 2025) = 29M adults; 47% worried about affordability
Notes: 11% cannot access quality care. "Cost desperate" = cannot afford AND cannot access. ACA subsidy lapse likely pushing this higher in 2026. Dental highest unmet need category.

Name: Rural Hospital Closure Rate
Description: Number of rural hospital closures / at-risk facilities
Current Value: 182 closed since 2010; 46% negative operating margins; 432 at risk; 18 closures in past year
Data Sources: Chartis 2025 State of Rural Health; Fierce Healthcare
Notes: ELEVATED. 46% of rural hospitals have negative operating margin. Non-expansion states 53% in red. Rural hospital loss = access desert for communities. Enhanced ACA subsidy loss costing rural hospitals $1.6B in patient revenue.

Name: Hospital System Operating Margin
Current Value: 1.3% median (Dec 2025); monthly 5% (including allocations); 2026 starting with "depressed margins"
Data Sources: Kaufman Hall National Hospital Flash Report Dec 2025
Notes: Margins recovering from 2022-23 collapse but remain thin. Gap between gross and net revenue indicates payer mix erosion (more Medicaid/uninsured). 2026 starting depressed. ACA subsidy lapse → more uncompensated care.

Name: ACA Marketplace Health
Description: ACA marketplace enrollment and coverage stability
Current Value: 23.1M (2026 OEP close) = -1.2M (-4.9%) vs 2025 record. 9% of prior enrollees now uninsured. CMS projects addl 750K-2M mid-year dropouts.
Data Sources: CMS 2026 OEP; KFF Jan 2026; CNBC Mar 2026; CMS mid-year analysis 2026
Notes: ACUTE 2026 TRIGGER. Enhanced subsidies expired. First enrollment decline since 2020. Urban Institute projects 4.8M total coverage loss. CMS itself flagged 750K-2M mid-year dropouts as premiums prove unaffordable. Fraud-related removals added 1.5M to decline. More than half of those who reenrolled cutting food/clothing to afford premiums. Watch: Q2-Q3 for mid-year attrition data.
